title: How to Find High-Intent B2B Prospects From Job Postings
summary: Find high-intent B2B prospects from job postings: start from your ICP accounts, pull recent careers-page roles, read the pain, and reach the real buyer.
body_markdown:
**Short answer:** To find high-intent B2B prospects from job postings, start with the accounts that already fit your ICP, not the whole job market. Pull each account's recent postings from its careers page, keep only roles that prove your problem exists, read each posting for the pain, the tools, and who the role reports to, and then contact that person. Re-run it weekly.


## Why start from your account list, not a job board?


Searching job boards by title gives you thousands of postings, and most are at companies you'd never sell to. Starting from a list of companies that already fit (industry, size, location, stack) flips the work: every posting you find is at an account you want. Fit is decided first, so the posting only has to answer one question: *are they in-market now?*


It also catches roles that never reach the big aggregators. Many startups post only on their own careers page or applicant tracking system (ATS).


If you'd rather go the other way and search by role across the market, Orange Slice has a ready-made[find companies hiring for specific roles](https://orangeslice.ai/use-cases/job-research/companies-hiring-specific-roles) workflow. Both approaches work. This post covers the account-first version.


## The five-column recipe


An agentic enrichment spreadsheet is a sheet where each column is an AI agent that does research on every row. Here's the job-postings play as five columns you can add to any account list.


**1. Careers page.** Find each company's careers URL from its domain. Orange Slice's[Find Careers Page](https://orangeslice.mintlify.app/services/company/find-careers) service takes a domain (plus the company LinkedIn URL for better accuracy) and returns the URL.


**2. Recent postings.** Scrape the listings and keep only fresh ones.[Scrape Jobs](https://orangeslice.mintlify.app/services/company/scrape-jobs) works with major ATS providers, including Workday, iCIMS, Greenhouse, Lever, and LinkedIn. It can filter to the last 24 hours, week, or month, and it can pull full descriptions.


**3. Trigger match.** Ask the column one plain question: "Is any open role one that a company posts right before it would buy \[your product\]?" Return the matching titles, or leave the cell empty.


**4. Intent read.** For each match, pull three lines from the description: the **pain sentence** ("build our outbound motion from scratch"), the **stack** (tools listed in the requirements), and the **reports-to line** , which usually names your buyer.[GTM Skills](https://www.gtmskills.com/skill/hiring-signal-prospecting) describes the same three-line read.


**5. Buyer + verified email.** Find the person named in "reports to" (often the founder at a small company) and verify their email. On Orange Slice, a work email is[charged only when one is found](https://orangeslice.ai/pricing) .


You don't have to wire these columns up by hand. On Orange Slice you[describe what you want in plain English](https://orangeslice.ai/) , and the agent builds the columns. A value with no source stays empty, so a blank "Intent read" cell means "no signal," not a guess.


## How do you tell a high-intent posting from noise?


A posting is high-intent when the role, the wording, and the timing all point to a problem you solve this quarter. A posting is noise when it's generic, old, or at the wrong company. Run every match through a quick filter:


Keep (higher intent) Drop or deprioritize


First hire in a function (first SDR, first RevOps) Generic backfills with no change in scope


Description names a pain you solve Boilerplate descriptions with no specifics


Requirements list a tool you replace or integrate with Agency or staffing-firm postings


Several related roles open at once Postings that have been open a long time with no repost


Recently posted or reposted Companies outside your ICP, however strong the signal


Our guide to[hiring signals for B2B prospecting](https://orangeslice.ai/blog/how-use-hiring-signals-b2b-prospecting) maps role types to the products they signal. The guide to[timing outreach with job posting data](https://orangeslice.ai/blog/job-posting-data-time-b2b-outreach) covers how fast to move once a posting goes live.


## Stack the posting with other buying signals


A job posting is strongest when it isn't alone. Add one or two more signal columns to the same sheet, such as recent funding, a leadership change, or a tech stack change, and sort by rows where several signals line up. Our post on[buying signals in B2B sales](https://orangeslice.ai/blog/buying-signals-b2b-sales) explains how to weight them.


## Make it a weekly habit


Postings change every week. Put the sheet on a schedule so new and reposted roles show up without a manual check. Orange Slice can[run the same prompt every week](https://orangeslice.ai/) and asks before it sends anything. For more plays like this, see[job and hiring research use cases](https://orangeslice.ai/use-cases/job-research) .


## FAQ


### How do I find high-intent B2B prospects from job postings?


Start from a list of companies that fit your ICP. Pull each one's recent postings from its careers page and keep roles that prove the problem you solve exists. Read each posting for the pain, the tools, and the reporting line, then contact the person the role reports to. Re-run weekly.


### Which job postings show the highest buying intent?


The strongest are first hires in a function, roles whose descriptions name a pain you solve, postings that list a tool you replace or integrate with, and several related roles opening at once. Generic backfills, agency postings, and roles at companies outside your ICP are usually noise.


### Should I search job boards or company careers pages?


Use both, for different jobs. Job boards help you discover new companies hiring for a role. Careers pages are better when you already have a target account list, because many smaller companies post only on their own site or ATS, and those roles may not show up on aggregators.


### Who should I contact when a company posts a relevant job?


Contact the budget owner, usually the person named in the posting's "reports to" line. At a small startup, that's often a founder. Don't contact the recruiter or the person being hired, since neither usually owns the purchase.


### Can I automate job-posting prospecting in a spreadsheet?


Yes. In an agentic enrichment spreadsheet like Orange Slice, each column is an AI agent: one finds the careers page, one pulls recent postings, one flags trigger roles, one reads the description, and one finds and verifies the buyer's email. You can run it on a schedule.


### Is a job posting enough on its own to prioritize an account?


No. Treat it as one buying signal. Postings can stay up after a role is filled or paused, so combine them with ICP fit and other signals, such as recent funding or a leadership change, before deciding who to contact first.
